akhfash:11-11.t: He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَانَ عَلَىٰ ٱلْهُدَىٰ﴾, then He said ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾: He made it a badal (substitute) for it, and made the khabar (predicate) ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ﴾.

akhfash:17-18.t: And He said ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ﴾ ﴿سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾: ﴿نادِيَهُ﴾ here is his clan, for they are the people of the nādī (assembly), and the nādī is his place and his gathering. As for ﴿الزّبانِيَةُ﴾, some said its singular is "الزَبانِي", and some said "الزَابِن" — I heard "الزابِن" from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar — and some said "الزِبْنِية". The Arabs hardly know this, and make it one of the plurals that have no singular, like "أَبابِيل": you say "جاءَتْ إِبِلِي أبابِيل" ("my camels came in flocks"), that is: in separate groups. This comes in the meaning of multiplicity, like "عَباديِد" and "شَعارِير".

celaleyn:1-1.t: Its opening, up to «ما لم يعلم», is the first of the Qur'an to be revealed, and that was in the cave of Ḥirāʾ; al-Bukhārī narrated it. ﴿اقْرَأْ﴾: bring about reading, beginning ﴿بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾ the creatures,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ﴾: the species ﴿مِنْ عَلَقٍ﴾: plural of «علقة», which is a small piece of thick blood.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿اقْرَأْ﴾: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first. ﴿وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ﴾, whom no generous one equals: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «اقرأ»,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿الَّذِي عَلَّمَ﴾ writing ﴿بِالْقَلَمِ﴾; the first to write with it was Idrīs, peace be upon him.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿عَلَّمَ الْإِنْسَانَ﴾: the species ﴿مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ﴾ before He taught him, of guidance, writing, crafts and other things.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿أَنْ رَآهُ﴾, that is, himself, ﴿اسْتَغْنَى﴾ through wealth. This was revealed concerning Abū Jahl. «رأى» is of knowing (ʿilmiyya), «استغنى» is the second object, and «أن رآه» is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّ إِلَى رَبِّكَ﴾, O man, ﴿الرُّجْعَى﴾, that is, the return: a warning to him; so the transgressor will be recompensed with what he deserves.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾ in the three places is for expressing wonder (taʿajjub). ﴿الَّذِي يَنْهَى﴾: he is Abū Jahl,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿عَبْدًا﴾: he is the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿إِذَا صَلَّى﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَانَ﴾, that is, the one forbidden, ﴿عَلَى الْهُدَى﴾

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ﴾, that is, the one forbidding [denied] the Prophet, ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ from faith,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى﴾ what has come from him, that is, He knows it and will recompense him for it? That is, wonder at him, O you addressed, in respect of his forbidding the prayer, and in respect of the one forbidden being on guidance and commanding piety, and in respect of the one forbidding being a denier who turns away from faith.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a deterrent (radʿ) to him. ﴿لَئِنْ﴾: the lām of the oath. ﴿لَمْ يَنْتَهِ﴾ from the disbelief he is in, ﴿لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ﴾: We will surely drag him by his forelock to the Fire,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿نَاصِيَةٍ﴾: an indefinite badal (substitute) from a definite noun. ﴿كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ﴾: describing it thus is figurative (majāz); what is meant is its owner.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ﴾, that is, the people of his nādī, which is the gathering place in which people meet and talk. He had said to the Prophet ﷺ, when [the Prophet] rebuked him as he forbade him from the prayer: "You know that there is no man here with a larger gathering than mine; I will fill this valley against you, if I wish, with sleek horses and beardless young men."

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾: the harsh, severe angels, to destroy him, as in the hadith: "Had he called his gathering, the zabāniya would have seized him in plain sight."

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a deterrent (radʿ) to him. ﴿لَا تُطِعْهُ﴾, O Muhammad, in abandoning the prayer, ﴿وَاسْجُدْ﴾: pray to Allah ﴿وَاقْتَرِبْ﴾ to Him through obeying Him.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿اقْرَأْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِاسْمِ﴾: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and ﴿اسم﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿الَّذِي﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ربك; ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause اقرأ… is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: badal (substitute) for the preceding one, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مِنْ عَلَقٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿اقْرَأْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause emphasizes the preceding one; ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of ربك; ﴿عَلَّمَ﴾: a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالْقَلَمِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿عَلَّمَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and it is a badal (substitute) for the preceding one; ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿ما﴾: second direct object; ﴿لَمْ يَعْلَمْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَيَطْغى﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿أَنْ رَآهُ﴾: an is a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the accusative, and a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); ﴿اسْتَغْنى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾: the fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿الرُّجْعى﴾: its postponed noun; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الَّذِي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿يَنْهى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿عَبْداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿صَلَّى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its noun latent (mustatir); ﴿عَلَى الْهُدى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿أَمَرَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالتَّقْوى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾: conjoined to كذب; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ﴾: ألم: the hamza is a particle of interrogation and affirmation (taqrīr), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; ﴿بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and anna and its noun; ﴿يَرى﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يعلم.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿لَئِنْ﴾: the lām is the one that prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and إن is a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿لَمْ يَنْتَهِ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the light nūn of emphasis, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالنَّاصِيَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position, and the clause لم ينته is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿ناصِيَةٍ﴾: badal (substitute) for الناصية; ﴿كاذِبَةٍ خاطِئَةٍ﴾: two adjectives (naʿt).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿نادِيَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿سَنَدْعُ﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw, which is dropped in recitation; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الزَّبانِيَةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿لا تُطِعْهُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; the hāʾ is its object and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَاسْجُدْ﴾: an imperative verb whose agent is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَاقْتَرِبْ﴾: conjoined to اسجد.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾.
This is the first of the Qur'an that was revealed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him.

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ﴾.
It was said «من علق», whereas it is [one] «علقةٌ» (clot), because «الإنسان» has a plural meaning; so «العلق» was taken as plural, to match the verse-endings.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ﴾.
He did not say: أن رأى نفسه (that he saw himself). When the Arabs make a verb that is satisfied with one noun [i.e. a verb with a single object] fall upon themselves, or make it fall from someone else upon himself, they put «نفس» in the place of the pronoun. So they say: قتلتَ نفسك (you killed yourself), and they do not say: قتلتَك or قتلته [for the same person]; and they say: قتل نفسَه (he killed himself) and قتلتُ نفسى (I killed myself). But when the verb requires a noun and a predicate (khabar), they drop «النفس» and say: متى تراك خارجاً (when do you consider yourself going out?) and متى نظنك خارجاً (when do we think you are going out?). [Translator's note: «نظنك» is as printed; the parallel with «تراك» suggests «تظنك» (when do you think yourself …).] And His word, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿أَن رَّآهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ﴾, is of this kind.

farraa:9-10.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ (9) عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ﴾.
It was revealed concerning Abū Jahl: he used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at his place of prayer, and harm him and forbid him; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِي يَنْهَىٰ عَبْداً إِذَا صَلَّىٰ﴾?, meaning the Prophet ﷺ.

farraa:13-13.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَرَأَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾.
There is an Arabic [construction] in it. Its like in ordinary speech would be if it were said: أرأيت الذى ينهى عبداً إذا صلّى وهو كاذب متولٍّ عن الذكر؟ (Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays, while he is lying and turning away from the Reminder?), i.e.: what could be more astonishing than this?

farraa:14-14.t:
Then He said — woe to him! — ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ﴾.
Meaning Abū Jahl. Then He said: ﴿كَلاَّ لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ﴾.
His forelock (ناصيته): the front of his head; i.e.: We shall surely bend it down, We shall surely seize it, We shall surely abase him and humiliate him. It is also said: We shall surely drag [him] by the forelock to the Fire, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِى والأَقْدَامِ﴾, and they are thrown into the Fire. It is also said: We shall surely blacken his face; so the forelock stood in for the face, because it is at the front of the face.

farraa:15-16.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَنَسْفَعاً بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ نَاصِيَةٍ﴾.
By repetition (takrīr, i.e. badal (substitute)), as He said: ﴿إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ، صِرَاطِ اللهِ﴾. The definite is made to follow the indefinite by repetition, and the indefinite the definite. Whoever puts (ناصيةً) in the accusative makes it an act of the definite [Translator's note: so the source, «جعله فعلا للمعرفة»; the sense appears to be that the accusative is governed with reference to the definite «الناصية», e.g. as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the wording may be corrupt], and it is permissible in reading.

farraa:17-18.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾.
They are stronger, and they work with hands and feet; and the she-camel تزْبِن (pushes off) the milker and kicks him with her foot.
Al-Kisāʾī said, later in life: the singular of «الزبانية» is زِبْنِىٌّ; before that he used to say: I have not heard a singular for it. And I do not know whether it was by analogy (qiyās) on his part or by hearing (samāʿ). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "كَلاَّ لئِن لَّمْ يَنْتَهِ لأسْفَعاً بِالنَّاصِيَةِ", and in it also: "فَلْيَدْعُ إلىّ نَادِيَه فَسَأَدْعُو الزَّبَانِيَة".

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: His saying «الذي»: naʿt (adjective) of «ربك»; the preposition «باسم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: read, beginning with the name.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «خلق» is a badal (substitute) of the preceding « {خَلَقَ} ».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «ربك الأكرم»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «الذي»: naʿt (adjective); the preposition «بالقلم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the bāʾ is that of seeking aid (istiʿāna).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «علَّم» is a badal (substitute) of the preceding one.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (أن رآه استغنى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām; the clause «استغنى» is the second object of the mental seeing; and the verb of the attached latent pronoun was made transitive to its own attached pronoun, and He did not say: أن رأى نفسه (that he saw himself).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (إن إلى ربك الرجعى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: His saying «الذي»: a relative noun, the first object of «أرأيت» in the sense of "tell me"; the second object is indicated by the interrogative clause in verse (14), which is the object of the third.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The first object of «رأيت» is a pronoun referring to {الَّذِي يَنْهَى}, which occurs as the object of the first «أرأيت»; the second object was omitted because the second object of the third «أرأيت» indicates it. Thus the second was omitted from the first, the first from the third, and both from the second; and that is of the kind of omission on account of indication. The clause «إن كان على الهدى» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the interrogative clause of the second object {أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى}.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: (ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) stands in place of the two objects of علم.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The lām is the preparatory one (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa), and «نَسْفَعَنْ» is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the light nūn of emphasis; the nūn has no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (فليدع ناديه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (اقرأ باسم ربك): the bāʾ entered upon (اسم) to indicate persistence and repetition; its like is "I took hold of the halter" (أخذت بالخطام). If you said "Read the name of your Lord" and "I took the halter", there would be nothing in the speech indicating the persistence and repetition of the action. The grammarians allowed (اقرأ يا هذا) with the hamza omitted, on the assumption that the hamza was replaced by an alif before the imperative [was formed], as He said (أتستبدلون الذي هو أدنى بالذي هو خير): the alif in (أدنى), according to a group, replaces a hamza, it being from (الدناءة) "baseness". When the imperative entered upon it, the alif [printed «اللف»] was dropped for the indeclinability. It is indeclinable (mabnī) according to the Basrans and declinable according to the Kufans.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (وربك الأكرم): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (اقرأ).

mekki-muskil:7-8.t:
His saying (أن رآه استغنى): (أن) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The hāʾ and (استغنى) are two objects of (رأى); (رأى) in the sense of knowing takes two objects. Qunbul read, from Ibn Kathīr, (أن رأه) without an alif after the hamza, as if he dropped the final radical, as it was dropped in (حاش لله). Its dropping is reported from the Arabs: it is reported (أصاب الناس) and (أوتر أهل مكة) [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably forms with a dropped final alif are meant], so they dropped the alif because the fatḥa indicates it. It has also been said that the hamza was lightened by substitution, so two alifs met, and the second was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; then when the word became deficient, the hamza was returned to its original. It is also said that the alif was dropped only because it is vowelless and the sīn after it is vowelless, since the hāʾ is a faint letter not taken into account; and the pause was run on the wording of the continuous reading, so it was dropped in the pause as it was dropped in the continuous reading, so that they would not differ. It is also said that the alif was dropped only because the imperfect of (رأى) has been used with its middle radical dropped after throwing its vowel onto what precedes it, a usage in which it became like the original, with nothing else permissible; so they said (نرى), (ترى) and (يرى). Then the past ran on that pattern, but dropping the middle radical was not possible, since there is no vowelless letter before it onto which the vowel could be thrown; so the final radical was dropped.
His saying (أرأيت): the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the tāʾ is presumably meant] is vowelless [i.e. the letter before the pronoun], and it may never take a vowel because the nominative pronoun is attached to it. Whoever does not pronounce the hamza in (أرأيت) makes the hamza between hamza and alif; it is also said that he replaced it with an alif; the first is the original.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying (لنسفعا): this nūn is the light nūn of emphasis, which entered together with the lām of the oath. The pause on it, when what precedes it has fatḥa, is with alif; and it is dropped in the pause when what precedes it has ḍamma or kasra, and what was dropped because of it is restored. If you said (الزيدون هل يقومن يا هذا) with the light nūn and then paused on it, you would restore the wāw, which is the sign of the pronoun, and restore the nūn, which is for the nominative, and say (هل يقومون). Likewise you say to a female (هل تضربن زيدا); if you pause, you restore [printed «وددت»] the yāʾ, which is the sign of the feminine, and restore the nūn, which is the sign of the nominative, and say (هل تضربين).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿اقرأ﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿باسم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the agent, i.e. "beginning" (مفتتحا); «اسم» is muḍāf.
﴿ربك﴾: the word ﴿رب﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra, and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿الذي﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رب﴾, in the position of genitive.
﴿خلق﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾, referring back to ﴿الذي﴾; the clause ﴿خلق﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿خلق﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being ﴿هو﴾, referring back to ﴿الذي﴾; the clause ﴿خلق الإنسان﴾ is a badal (substitute) for the preceding ﴿خلق﴾, or verbal tawkīd (emphasis).
﴿الإنسان﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿من علق﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلق﴾.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿اقرأ﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت); this «اقرأ» is an emphasis of the first ﴿اقرأ﴾.
﴿وربك﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), «رب» is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿الأكرم﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿اقرأ﴾ is resumptive for emphasis, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿وربك الأكرم﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of ﴿اقرأ﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الأكرم﴾, or in the position of nominative as a second khabar (predicate) of ﴿ربك﴾.
﴿علم﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "He" (هو), referring back to Allah, and its two objects are omitted, i.e. "He taught man writing by the pen" (علّم الإنسان الخطَّ بالقلم); the clause ﴿عَلَّم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿بالقلم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿علم﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿علم﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "He" (هو), referring back to Allah.
﴿الإنسان﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa. The clause ﴿علّم الإنسان﴾ is an emphasis of the first ﴿علم﴾, or a badal (substitute), or a khabar (predicate).
﴿ما لم يعلم﴾: «ما» is a relative noun, second mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ﴿لم يعلم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. The returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "he did not know it" (لم يعلمه).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إن الإنسان﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle, and «الإنسان» is its noun (ism).
﴿ليطغى﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «يطغى» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent's implied form is "he" (هو); the clause ﴿يطغى﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; it together with what it governs is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
﴿رآه﴾: ﴿رآ﴾ is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿استغنى﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif; the clause ﴿استغنى﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ refers back to man (الإنسان).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle.
﴿إلى ربك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿الرجعى﴾: the postponed noun (ism) of «إن»; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿أرأيت﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of wonder (taʿajjubī), and «رأى» is an indeclinable (mabnī) past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أرأيت﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ينهى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is "he" (هو); the second object of ﴿رأيت﴾ is omitted, and it is an interrogative clause indicated by His saying ﴿ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى﴾; the clause ﴿ينهى﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿عبدا﴾: the object of ﴿ينهى﴾.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, purely adverbial, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينهى﴾.
﴿صلى﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿أرأيت﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of wonder (taʿajjubī), and «رأى» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أرأيت﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿إن﴾: conditional.
﴿كان﴾: a deficient past verb, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its noun (ism) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿على الهدى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of «كان»; the clause ﴿إن كان على الهدى﴾ is parenthetical, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿أمر﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and its fāʿil (agent) is ﴿هو﴾; conjoined to ﴿كان على الهدى﴾.
﴿بالتقوى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أمر﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿أرأيت﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of wonder (taʿajjubī), and «رأى» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أرأيت﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿إن﴾: conditional.
﴿كذب﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿وتولى﴾: conjoined to ﴿كذب﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿يعلم﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm).
﴿بأن﴾: the bāʾ is for the genitive and «أن» is maṣdariyya.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, the noun (ism) of ﴿أن﴾.
﴿يرى﴾: an imperfect verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir); the clause of verb and agent is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن الله يرى﴾ is genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يعلم﴾, and the clause ﴿ألم يعلم﴾ is in the position of accusative as the second object of the first ﴿رأيت﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿كلا﴾: deterrence and rebuke.
﴿لئن﴾: the lām paves the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and «إن» is conditional.
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿ينته﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter.
﴿لنسفعا﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of the oath, and «نسفعا» is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the light nūn of emphasis, which is written with an alif in the Muṣḥaf according to the rule of pausing; the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "We" (نحن); the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer of the oath indicates it and fulfils its meaning.
﴿بالناصية﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نسفعا﴾.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿ناصية﴾: a badal (substitute) for ﴿الناصية﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿كاذبة خاطئة﴾: two naʿts (adjectives) of ﴿ناصية﴾, genitive.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿فليدع﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa), the lām is the lām of command, and «يدع» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the wāw, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿ناديه﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿سندع﴾: the sīn is a particle of the future, and «ندعو» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the wāw, which was dropped for lightness, and the agent is ﴿نحن﴾.
﴿الزبانية﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿كلا﴾: an emphasis of the deterrence and rebuke.
﴿لا﴾: prohibitive, governing the jussive.
﴿تطعه﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿واسجد﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿واقترب﴾: conjoined to ﴿واسجد﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ: (اقرأ) is in the position of the jussive (jazm) on the view of the Kufans; the operator in it according to al-Farrāʾ is an omitted lām, and the mark of the jussive is the dropping of the ḍamma. According to the Basrans it is not declinable (muʿrab), because it does not resemble nouns so as to be declined. Abū Zayd and al-Kisāʾī reported «اقرَ» with substitution of the hamza, so that it becomes like your saying اخش. And the like of this is the saying of Zuhayr: [al-Ṭawīl] 578- وإن لا يبد بالظّلم يظلم ("and if he does not begin with wrongdoing, he is wronged"). It has been said that on this basis is the reading of the community أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنى بِالَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ [al-Baqara: 61], and that it is taken from danāʾa (baseness).
الَّذِي خَلَقَ is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ربك, or in the position of the nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject), or in the position of the accusative with the sense of "I mean".

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: I.e., along with his preventing (him) from prayer, if he denied Allah and His Messenger and turned away from obeying Him.

nahhas-irab:14-16.t:
أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرى (14), i.e., sees him and knows his deed and will punish him for it. And whoever says كَلَّا is the complete stop says:
The meaning is: the matter is not as he reckoned, that it would be possible for him to prevent him from praying. لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ: the yāʾ was dropped for the jussive, and whoever retains it outside the Qur'an assumes it to be vowelled. لَنَسْفَعاً: the pause on it is with alif, to distinguish between it and the heavy nūn, and because it is in the rank of your saying رأيت زيدا, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 579- ولا تحمد الشّيطان والله فاحمدا ("and do not praise Satan, but Allah — praise Him!"). بِالنَّاصِيَةِ ناصِيَةٍ كاذِبَةٍ خاطِئَةٍ (16):
(ناصية is) a badal (substitute); al-Farrāʾ (takes it) as repetition. And he permitted ناصِيَةٍ كاذِبَةٍ خاطِئَةٍ [Translator's note: the printed vowelling is the standard one; what al-Farrāʾ permitted is the accusative, ناصيةً كاذبةً خاطئةً], because it is indefinite after a definite.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: فَلْيَدْعُ نادِيَهُ (17): the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place by way of extension (ittisāʿ), i.e., the people of his assembly.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: It was written without wāw according to the connected pronunciation (idrāj), and it is not permissible to pause on it.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: كَلَّا لا تُطِعْهُ, i.e., in what he forbids you of, out of error; وَاسْجُدْ وَاقْتَرِبْ to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by obeying Him, for He will exalt you and protect you. In the ḥadīth: «The closest a servant is to Allah the Exalted is when he is prostrating, so make much supplication in prostration, for it is fitting that you be answered».

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: الإنسان is in the sense of a group (i.e., collective); therefore He said علق, which is the plural of ʿalaqa (clinging clot).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The mafʿūl bihi (direct object) was omitted, i.e., "Read what has been sent down to you, and your Lord, the Most Generous, will not leave you without reward for your reading".

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: A naʿt (adjective) of the first الذي.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t: عَلَّمَ الْإِنْسانَ ما لَمْ يَعْلَمْ (5): two objects. And whoever says that كَلَّا is a complete stop throughout the whole Qur'an says: the meaning is: they ought not to abandon reflecting on what Allah has made clear of your creation, which indicates His oneness and that He has no likeness. إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَيَطْغى: it came on the pattern faʿala yafʿalu because it contains the ghayn (a guttural letter).

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: So the object came attached (as a pronoun referring to the subject), and رأى نفسه was not used, because it is one of the sisters of ẓanantu (verbs of thinking).

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (الرجعى is) in the position of the accusative, and the case-inflection is not visible in it because there is an alif at its end.

nahhas-irab:9-12.t: أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يَنْهى (9) عَبْداً إِذا صَلَّى (10): the answer was omitted because the hearer knows it; and likewise أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كانَ عَلَى الْهُدى (11) أَوْ أَمَرَ بِالتَّقْوى (12).

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {اقرأ}: The majority read with sukūn on the hamza, as an imperative from القراءة (reading). ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of al-Aʿshā, read it with a fatḥa-voweled rāʾ [and no hamza], as though he changed the hamza into an alif, as in their saying قرا يَقْرا, like سعَى يَسْعى; then, when he formed the imperative from it, he omitted the alif in the same way as it is omitted from اسْعَ. This is like the saying of Zuhayr:
4603 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وإلاَّ يُبْدَ بالظُّلْمِ يُظْلَمِ
(…and if he does not begin with wrongdoing, he will be wronged.)
Its exposition has already been given.
His saying: {باسم رَبِّكَ}: Several views are possible on it. The first: the bāʾ is circumstantial (for the ḥāl), i.e. read, beginning with the name of your Lord: say "In the name of Allah", then read. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being: read the name of your Lord, as in his saying:
4604 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سُوْدُ المَحاجِرِ لا يَقْرَأْنَ بالسُّوَرِ
(…dark around the eyes, they do not recite the sūras.)
It was also said: the [word] «اسم» is redundant (ṣila), i.e. remember your Lord. Abū ʿUbayda said both of these. The third: the bāʾ is for seeking aid (istiʿāna) and the object is omitted, its implied form being: read what is revealed to you, seeking aid by the name of your Lord. The fourth: it is in the sense of «على», i.e. read upon the name of your Lord, as in His saying: {وَقَالَ اركبوا فِيهَا بِسْمِ الله} [Hūd: 41]; al-Akhfash said this. It has already been discussed at the beginning of this work how this verb was placed before the preposition [here] while it was supplied as coming after it in «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم», together with people's explanations of that, so that suffices instead of repeating it.
His saying: {الذي خَلَقَ خَلَقَ الإنسان}: The second «خَلَقَ» may be an explanation of the first «خَلَقَ», meaning that He left it vague at first and then explained it secondly by the creation of man, to magnify the creation of man. It is also possible that He omitted the object from the first, its implied form being: He created everything, because it is unrestricted and so covers every created thing.

semin-durr:2-2.t: And His saying: {خَلَقَ الإنسان}: a singling out of him for mention among all that creation covers, because the revelation is [sent down] to him. It may also be a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī), in which case He would have emphasised the ṣila (relative clause) alone, as in your saying: «الذي قام قام زيدٌ» (the one who stood — Zayd stood). What is meant by الإنسان is the genus; that is why He said: {مِنْ عَلَقٍ}, the plural of عَلَقة (clinging clot), because each one is created from a clot, as in the other verse.

semin-durr:4-4.t: And His saying: {الذى عَلَّمَ بالقلم عَلَّمَ الإنسان مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ}: close to His saying: «خَلَق، خلَق الإِنسانَ», so you may apply here again what has preceded.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {أَن رَّآهُ}: «أنْ» [with its clause] is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. because he sees himself as self-sufficient. The verb here passes over to its two attached pronouns [subject and object referring to the same person], because this is among the special features of this class [of verbs]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The meaning of seeing is knowing; had it been in the sense of seeing with the eyes, combining the two pronouns would be prohibited with its verb; and "استغنى" is the second object.» I say: there is disagreement on the question. A group held that «رأى» of eyesight is given the ruling of «رأى» of knowledge, and they counted among this the saying of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: «لقد رَأَيْتُنا مع رسولِ الله ﷺ وما لنا طعامٌ إلاَّ الأسْوَدان» (we saw ourselves with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ having no food but the two black things), and he quoted:
4605 - ولقد أَراني للرِّماح دَرِيْئَةً ... مِنْ عَنْ يمين تارةً وأمامي
(I have seen myself as a target for the spears, at times from my right and [at times] before me.)
Its verification has already been given. Qunbul — with disagreement [among the transmitters] from him — read «رَأَه» without an alif after the hamza; it is shortened from «رآه» in the reading of the majority. There is no doubt that omission in such a case has occurred rarely, as in their saying: «اصابَ الناسَ جَهْدٌ، ولو تَرَ أهلَ مكةَ» (hardship befell the people — if only you saw the people of Mecca), with omission of the final radical of «ترى», and the saying of the other:
4606 - وَصَّانِيَ العَجَّاجُ فيما وَصَّني ...
(Al-ʿAjjāj enjoined me in what he enjoined me.)
meaning: وصَّاني. When Ibn Mujāhid related this reading from Qunbul — and he said: «I read it so before him» — he attributed it to error. [Translator's note: the text reads «الغلظ» (coarseness), evidently for «الغلط» (error); translated accordingly.] That is not proper, because when a reading is established and has a valid rationale, even if another is better known than it, one should not venture to declare it erroneous.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {أَرَأَيْتَ الذي}: The discussion of this word has already been given to you in full. Al-Zamakhsharī has a discussion here which I saw fit to mention because of a particularity relating to it. He said: «If you say: what is the object of "أَرَأَيْت"? I say: "الذي يَنْهى" together with the conditional clause; they are in the position of the two objects. If you say: then where is the apodosis (jawāb) of the condition? I say: it is omitted, its implied form being: if he is upon guidance or commands piety, does he not know that Allah sees? It was omitted only because its mention in the apodosis of the second condition indicates it. If you say: how is it valid for "ألم يعلَمْ" to be the apodosis of the condition? I say: just as it is valid in your saying: "إنْ أَكْرَمْتُك أتكرِمُني" (if I honour you, will you honour me?) and "إن أَحْسَنَ إليك زيدٌ هل تُحْسِنُ إليه؟" (if Zayd does good to you, will you do good to him?). If you say: then what is the second "أَرَأَيْتَ" and its coming between the two objects of "أَرَأَيْتَ"? I say: it is redundant (zāʾida), repeated for emphasis.» I say: since he has entered into discussing this verse, let us go along with him.
Know that «أرَأَيْتَ» — as you have learned — has as its second object only an interrogative clause, as in His saying: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُهُ} [Yūnus: 50] to its end, and similar cases are many. Here «أرَأَيْتَ» occurs three times, and after the third of them an interrogative clause is stated explicitly, so it is in the position of its second object; its first object is omitted, and it is a pronoun referring to «الذي ينهى», which occurs as the first object of the first «أَرَأَيْتَ». The object of the first «أَرَأيْتَ» that is the second [object] is omitted, and it is an interrogative clause like the clause occurring after the third «أَرَأَيْتَ». As for the second «أرأَيْتَ», no object is mentioned for it, neither first nor second: the first was omitted because the object of the first «أَرَأَيْتَ» indicates it, and the second was omitted because the object of the third «أَرَأَيْتَ» indicates it. So the second [object] was omitted from the first, the first from the third, and both from the second. The demand of each «أَرَأَيْتَ» for the nominal clause is not by way of contention (tanāzuʿ), because that calls for an implied pronoun, and clauses are not implied as pronouns — only single words are; rather, it is of the class of omission because of an indication. [Translator's note: «الجملة الاسمية» (the nominal clause) is as written; the preceding argument concerns the interrogative clause (الاستفهامية).] As for the discussion of the condition together with this «أَرَأَيْتَ», you have learned it from what is in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām, so we will not lengthen the discussion by repeating it. [Translator's note: the text reads «في نُطيل», evidently for «فلا نُطيل».] Al-Zamakhsharī's allowing the apodosis of the condition to be an interrogative by itself is not permissible; rather, they stipulated that the fāʾ must be mentioned in such a case, and if anything [to the contrary] occurs, it is poetic licence (ḍarūra).

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {لَنَسْفَعاً}: In pause, this nūn is pronounced as an alif, likening it to tanwīn; and likewise it is omitted after a ḍamma and a kasra in pause. Here it is written as an alif, following the pause. It is related from Abū ʿAmr: «لَنَسْفَعَنَّ» with the heavy nūn. السَّفْع is seizing and grasping a thing firmly and dragging it. ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib said:
4607 - قومٌ إذا سَمِعُوا الصَّريخَ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ... ما بين مُلْجمِ مُهْرِه أو سافعِ
(A people who, when they hear the cry for help, you see them either bridling their colts or seizing [their forelocks].)
It was also said: it is "taking" in the dialect of Quraysh. Al-Rāghib said: «السَّفْع is seizing the horse by its سُفْعة, i.e. the blackness of its forelock. With regard to blackness the hearthstones were called "سُفْع", and "به سُفْعَةُ غَضَبٍ" (he has a flush of anger), with regard to the smoky colour that comes over the face of one whose anger has become intense; and the falcon was called "أسْفَعُ" because of the glints of black in it; and a woman سَفْعاءُ اللونِ (dark-complexioned).» End of quotation. In the ḥadīth: «فقامَتِ امرأةٌ سَفْعاءُ الخَدَّيْن» (a woman with dark cheeks stood up).

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ}: a badal (substitute) from «الناصية», the substitution of an indefinite for a definite. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Its substitution for the definite, while it is indefinite, was permissible because it is described [by an adjective], so it conveys a meaning on its own.» I say: this is the doctrine of the Kufans; they do not permit substituting an indefinite for something else except on condition that it is described or that it has the same wording as the first; the doctrine of the Basrans stipulates nothing, and they quoted:
4608 - فلا وأبيك خيرٍ منك إنِّي ... لَيُوْذِيْنيْ التَّحَمْحُمُ والصَّهيلُ
(No, by your father — one better than you — the neighing and whinnying do trouble me.)
Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ناصيةً كاذبةً خاطئةً» in the accusative, by way of reviling (shatm). Al-Kisāʾī, in one transmission, read it in the nominative, on the implied [mubtadaʾ]: "it is a forelock". Lying and sinning were attributed to it figuratively. The alif and lām in «الناصية» — it was said: they compensate for the annexation, i.e. "by his forelock"; it was also said: the pronoun is omitted, i.e. "the forelock of him".

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ}: This is either by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the people of his assembly, or by figurative usage in calling the assembly, because it contains the people, as in His saying: {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82]. النادي and النَّدِيّ are the gathering place taken for conversation. Zuhayr said:
4609 - وفيهم مَقاماتٌ حِسانٌ وجوهُهُمْ ... وأَنْدِيَةٌ يَنْتابُها القولُ والفِعْلُ
(Among them are gatherings of fair-faced men, and assemblies frequented by [wise] word and deed.)
A Bedouin woman said: «He is the chief of his assembly and the support of those seeking his favour.»

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {الزبانية}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: «الزَّبانية in the speech of the Arabs are the police (shuraṭ); the singular is زِبْنِيَة like عِفْرِية, from الزَّبْن, which is pushing. It was also said: زِبْنيّ, as though it were related to الزَّبْن and then altered for the relation (nisba), as in their saying إمْسيّ; its origin is زَبانيّ, and then زبانِيَة was said by way of compensation.» ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash said: «Its singular is زابِن.» It was also said: it has no singular from its own wording, like عَباديد and شماطيط. The upshot is that the root denotes pushing. He said:
4610 - مطاعيمُ في القُصْوى مطاعينُ في الوغَى ... زبانيَةٌ غُلْبٌ عِظامٌ حُلُومُها
(Feeders [of guests] in the hardest times, thrusters [with spears] in battle, mighty repellers, thick-necked, great in their forbearance.)
Another said:
4611 - ومُسْتَعْجِبٍ مِمَّا يرى مِنْ أناتِنا ... ولو زَبَنَتْه الحَرْبُ لم يَتَرَمْرَمِ
(Many a one marvels at the patience he sees in us; yet had war pushed him, he would not have uttered a word.)
ʿUtba said: «War has pushed us and we have pushed it.» From it is الزُّبون (customer), because he is pushed from one seller to another. The majority read «سَنَدْعُ» with the nūn of majesty; it is not written with a wāw, and its parallel has already been given, as in «يَدْعُ الداعِ». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «سيدعى الزبانيةُ» as passive, with «الزَّبانية» in the nominative because it stands in place of the fāʿil (agent).

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ): it is said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), as in the poet's words:
لَا يَقْرَأْنَ بِالسُّورِ
(they do not recite the sūras).
It is also said that it entered to draw attention to beginning with His name in everything, as the Exalted said: «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ». On this view it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «اقْرَأْ مُبْتَدِئًا بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ» (recite, beginning with the name of your Lord).

ukberi-tibyan:6-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ لَيَطْغَى (٦) أَنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنَى (٧)).
The words of the Exalted (أَنْ رَآهُ): it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. he transgresses because of that.
The seeing (al-ruʾya) here is in the sense of knowing, so «اسْتَغْنَى» is the second object.

ukberi-tibyan:15-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنَّاصِيَةِ (١٥) نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ (١٦)).
The words of the Exalted (لَنَسْفَعًا): when one pauses on this nūn, an alif is substituted for it, because it is vowelless and the letter before it carries a fatḥa. (نَاصِيَةٍ) is a badal (substitute) for «النَّاصِيَةِ»; substituting an indefinite noun for a definite one became acceptable because the indefinite noun is qualified by an adjective (naʿt).

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ (١٧) سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ (١٨)).
The words of the Exalted (فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ): that is, the people of his assembly. «زَبَانِيَة» is of the pattern «فَعَالِيَة», from «الزَّبْن», which is pushing.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-ʿAlaq
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾ ("recite in the name of your Lord Who created"): it has come in the exegesis that the first verse of the Qur'an to be revealed was ﴿اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ﴾.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿الَّذِي عَلَّمَ بِالقَلَمِ﴾ ("Who taught by the pen"): that is, Who taught writing.

zajjaj:6-7.t: And His saying: ﴿كَلا إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَيَطْغى﴾ ﴿أنْ رَآهُ اسْتَغْنى﴾ ("nay, the human being surely transgresses, because he sees himself self-sufficient"): this was revealed about Abū Jahl ibn Hishām; and likewise ﴿أرَأيْتَ الَّذِي يَنْهى﴾ [al-ʿAlaq: 9] ﴿عَبْدًا إذا صَلّى﴾ [al-ʿAlaq: 10] ("have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays?"), because Abū Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad praying, I will tread on his neck."

zajjaj:15-15.t: And His saying: ﴿كَلا لَئِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًا بِالنّاصِيَةِ﴾ ("nay, if he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock"): that is, We will surely drag his forelock to the Fire. One says ”سَفَعْتُ بِالشَّيْءِ“ when I have grasped something and pulled it violently.

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying: ﴿ناصِيَةٍ كاذِبَةٍ خاطِئَةٍ﴾ ("a lying, sinning forelock"): its interpretation is "by a forelock whose owner is lying and sinning", just as one says ”فُلانٌ نَهارُهُ صائِمٌ، ولَيْلُهُ قائِمٌ“ ("so-and-so, his day is fasting and his night is standing in prayer"), the meaning being "he fasts in his day and stands in prayer in his night".

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿فَلْيَدْعُ نادِيَهُ﴾ ("then let him call his assembly"): its meaning is: let him call the people of his assembly, i.e. the people of his gathering, who were his clan; that is, let him seek their help.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبانِيَةَ﴾ ("We will call the zabāniya"): ”اَلزَّبانِيَةُ“ are the harsh and severe ones; their singular is ”زِبْنِيَةٌ“. Here they are the angels; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أنْفُسَكم وأهْلِيكم نارًا وقُودُها النّاسُ والحِجارَةُ عَلَيْها مَلائِكَةٌ غِلاظٌ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 6] ("O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are harsh angels"), and they are the zabāniya.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿كَلا﴾: that is, the matter is not as Abū Jahl holds. ﴿لا تُطِعْهُ واسْجُدْ واقْتَرِبْ﴾ ("do not obey him; prostrate and draw near"): that is, and draw near to your Lord through obedience.
